speaker: Lena
text: Okay, let's get started. Welcome to the sprint 14 review, everyone.

speaker: Lena
text: Omar is going to demo the new search feature first, then Priya has the numbers.

speaker: Omar
text: Thanks. So the big thing this sprint is that the assistant can finally answer from customer docs.

speaker: Omar
text: We built it with RAG, so the model looks up the relevant pages before it writes an answer.

speaker: Lena
text: And that's what stopped it from making up policy details last week?

speaker: Omar
text: Exactly. It quotes the source now, and it says so when it can't find anything.

speaker: Omar
text: All the documents are chunked and stored in a vector database, so search works by meaning, not keywords.

speaker: Priya
text: Which one did we pick in the end? I saw two invoices.

speaker: Omar
text: We kept the managed one. The self-hosted trial is shut down as of Monday.

speaker: Lena
text: Good. How fast is it for a real user?

speaker: Omar
text: Our p95 latency is 1.8 seconds, so nineteen out of twenty answers arrive faster than that.

speaker: Lena
text: The target in the roadmap was two seconds, right?

speaker: Omar
text: Yes, and we were at 3.4 two sprints ago, so this is a big jump.

speaker: Priya
text: What changed? Did we just buy bigger machines?

speaker: Omar
text: Partly the opposite. We applied quantization, which shrinks the model so it runs on cheaper GPUs.

speaker: Priya
text: And the answers didn't get worse?

speaker: Omar
text: On our test set the drop is under one percent. Nobody on the support team noticed.

speaker: Lena
text: And the tone? Customers complained it sounded too robotic.

speaker: Omar
text: We trained a small LoRA on two thousand of our best support replies, so it writes in our house style.

speaker: Omar
text: Training took four hours on a single GPU, instead of retraining the whole model.

speaker: Lena
text: Love it. So when can customers actually use this?

speaker: Omar
text: It's merged and deployed already, but nobody sees it yet.

speaker: Omar
text: It's behind a feature flag, so we can switch it on per customer without a new release.

speaker: Lena
text: Let's turn it on for the five design partners this week.

speaker: Omar
text: Agreed. Then we widen it slowly.

speaker: Lena
text: What does slowly mean in practice?

speaker: Omar
text: A canary release: five percent of traffic first, and if error rates stay flat, we go to everyone.

speaker: Priya
text: What happens if the five percent breaks?

speaker: Omar
text: We roll back in under a minute. It's one switch.

speaker: Lena
text: What about the Monday morning spike? That's when everyone logs in.

speaker: Omar
text: Autoscaling handles it. The cluster adds servers when traffic climbs and removes them at night.

speaker: Priya
text: So we only pay for the busy hours. Good.

speaker: Omar
text: There's one catch: the first request on a fresh server is slow.

speaker: Lena
text: How slow?

speaker: Omar
text: The cold start is about eight seconds while the model loads into memory, so we keep two servers warm.

speaker: Priya
text: Moving on to security. The bank pilot won't sign until we have SOC 2.

speaker: Lena
text: {listener}, can you own the SOC 2 questionnaire and get a first draft to Priya by Friday?

speaker: Priya
text: The auditor says the report takes about three months, so we need to start now.

speaker: Lena
text: What else are they asking for?

speaker: Priya
text: Access reviews, written policies, and proof that we test our own defences.

speaker: Priya
text: So we've booked a pen test for December, where an outside firm tries to break into the product.

speaker: Omar
text: I'll freeze the staging environment for them that week.

speaker: Lena
text: Great. Priya, can you take us through the numbers?

speaker: Priya
text: Sure. Revenue grew eleven percent this month, mostly from the two new mid-size accounts.

speaker: Priya
text: Marketing spent forty-two thousand dollars this month and we signed fourteen new customers.

speaker: Priya
text: That puts our CAC at about three thousand dollars per customer, down from four.

speaker: Priya
text: Churn is the worry. Three customers cancelled this month, two of them in their first ninety days.

speaker: Lena
text: Do we know why?

speaker: Priya
text: Both said setup was too hard. Nobody on our side helped them get started.

speaker: Lena
text: That's an onboarding problem, not a product problem. Let's add a setup call to every new contract.

speaker: Omar
text: Search will help there too, if the help docs answer setup questions.

speaker: Priya
text: On cash: at the current spend we have nineteen months of runway, so we're fine until mid next year.

speaker: Lena
text: Investors keep asking whether we're spending efficiently. What do we tell them?

speaker: Priya
text: We spend about one dollar sixty for each new dollar of yearly revenue we add.

speaker: Lena
text: Is that good?

speaker: Priya
text: It's okay for our stage. Below two is what the board wants to see.

speaker: Priya
text: That number is our burn multiple, and I want it closer to one by the next board meeting.

speaker: Lena
text: Okay. Let's wrap up with owners for next sprint.

speaker: Omar
text: {listener}, can you send me the pen test scope by Wednesday so I can prepare staging?

speaker: Omar
text: I'll own the canary rollout and send a daily error report.

speaker: Priya
text: I'll draft the onboarding call script with the support team.

speaker: Lena
text: And I'll talk to the design partners about switching on search.

speaker: Lena
text: Thanks, everyone. Great sprint. See you next week.
